svg.title: Temperatures on a logarithmic scale
svg.desc: A vertical logarithmic temperature axis in kelvin from 10⁻¹⁰ K to 10¹² K, each tick a factor of ten higher. Marked, from the bottom: the lowest temperature achieved (about 10⁻¹⁰ K), the Boomerang Nebula (1 K), liquid helium (4 K), liquid nitrogen (77 K), Vostok, Antarctica (183 K), water freezing (273 K) and boiling (373 K), a fireplace fire (about 1200 K), the solar surface and the center of the Earth (about 6000 K), the solar corona (about 10⁶ K), the solar interior (about 10⁷ K), rapid hydrogen fusion (10⁸ K), the interior of a neutron star (10⁹ K), and experiments at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (about 4 × 10¹² K).
